mode: Five separate calls, each with one official source image as direct visual reference
scope: Five primary logo reinterpretations only. No website or mockups.
status: AI reinterpretation candidates, user selection pending; not final vector artwork.
sources: Official Pink Floyd album pages and the image URLs linked from those pages. Downloaded as design references for the user-requested reinterpretation, not as production website assets. Source artwork retains its original authorship; no official endorsement or reuse license has been established.

inspection.01: Prism and rays clear; needs stronger personal differentiation.
inspection.02: Handshake recognizable; finger and wrist detail remains denser than preferred.
inspection.03: LSSH text legible with The Wall-derived lettering; preferred by executor for personal identity.
inspection.04: Two profiles and frontal face relation apparent; retains literal cover identity and mask-like expression.
inspection.05: Nested-window spatial relation apparent; inner frame is open, interpretation is simplified.
inspection.all: Images inspected visually; image pixels unmodified after generation. Small sizes and vector geometry not verified.

records.album: The Dark Side of the Moon
records.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand. Make ONE PRIMARY LOGO for the personal website Little Stone Still Here (LSSH), as a direct fan-art reinterpretation of the attached Pink Floyd artwork. The user explicitly requests recognizable derivation from Pink Floyd design. It must actually retain a key recognizable formal idea from this source, rather than just an unrelated shape given a poetic explanation. The output is a highly reduced, beautiful, memorable graphic logo, NOT an album cover, scene, illustration or poster. Adopt the source's compositional intelligence and rebuild its geometry for this personal identity. Extremely economical shapes, precise and intentional negative spaces, consistent visual weight, gentle corners and restrained proportions. No swollen biomorphic blobs, no decorative tiny details. Pure FLAT white graphic ink on pure FLAT black. No rendering, highlights, shadows, material, texture, gradients, colored lighting or mockups. A single centered mark occupying around 48% of a square black canvas, generous space. No explanatory text, no caption, no album title, no band name, no labels or other logo variants. Only produce the single resolved primary mark.

Reference role: the attached Dark Side of the Moon cover is the direct formal source. Retain the instantly recognizable relationship of an upright triangular prism, one incoming ray from the left, and light emerging to the right. Redraw it as a compact modern monoline emblem with pleasantly eased apex and corners, a confident simple triangle contour, one incoming white ray and THREE restrained short outgoing white rays. Keep all lines thick enough to be actual logo strokes, not hairlines. The overall graphic must be compact and balanced, not a panorama with long rays; the triangular 'little stone' is the dominant object. Allow the entering ray to share one short contour with the prism so the pieces are integrated as one authored mark. No rainbow, no glass, no additional dot or monogram. The transformation for LSSH: a small stable object receives the world and returns several directions of expression. One quiet, precise line-based symbol, noticeably redrawn and reduced from the cover.

Reduce each hand to only a few connected broad flat shapes, with one or two useful negative cuts suggesting fingers; no knuckles, screws, cables or anatomical detailing. Artful restrained geometric curves, no thick sticker border. The two simplified hands should be identifiable as an intentional robotic handshake, while together forming a single compact near-diamond silhouette. Keep a clear tiny breathing seam at the contact. LSSH meaning: meeting someone through what they leave behind. No letters or circular enclosing badge. A white silhouette logo on black, not a line drawing of machinery.

Reference role: the attached The Wall cover is the direct formal source, SPECIFICALLY ITS handwritten lettering. Produce the exact letters "LSSH" as one compact horizontal primary wordmark. Reinterpret the source's distinctive spontaneous ink lettering and long expressive strokes for these four letters, while making it much calmer, simpler and more coherent. Preserve the human hand and gentle irregular rhythm; use four readily legible uppercase letters with controlled brush-weight variation and very few strokes. L is the leading anchor, two S characters have fluid clear counters, H is the ending anchor. Soften harsh scratchy extremes while retaining the recognizable Pink Floyd / The Wall graphic lineage. No brick background, no illustrated wall, no extra symbol, no decorative underline, no pen marks, no distressed texture, no imitation text saying Pink Floyd. White clean silhouette ink lettering on black. Not a generic geometric computer font, not ornate script, not a heavy metal logo. Only LSSH.

Reference role: the attached The Division Bell cover is the direct formal source. Preserve its perceptual idea: TWO facing profiles together read as ONE frontal face. Translate the paired sculpture into an exceptionally reduced white-on-black emblem. Two balanced vertical stone-like silhouettes, with a shared central breathing gap; just enough forehead, nose and chin contour to read two people in conversation, and only the minimum paired eye cuts to allow the larger face to emerge. Strip all rivets, eyeballs, irises, metal texture, lips, neck muscles, landscape and lighting. No literal small statue drawing. Calm geometric human warmth, slightly eased contours, a strong compact outer silhouette; avoid a sinister mask, skull, cartoon, robot helmet or angry eyes. Deliberately redesign the head proportions and contour rather than tracing the photo. For LSSH this shared face is built from the author and the visitor; identity emerges in their encounter. One radically distilled graphic symbol. No letters.
